task: Facts from our infra team about the internal CI runners that build our Go fork: the runners run Linux kernel 5.4, and their seccomp profile blocks the pidfd_open syscall (it returns EPERM). Check whether os/exec or os process handling in this tree depends on pidfd, and whether there is a fallback when pidfd_open fails. Tell me what you found.

Decision from our runtime lead today: every service built from our fork will run with GODEBUG=disablethp=1, because our production hosts have transparent huge pages set to 'always' and several services showed RSS growth after the Go upgrade. We will not patch the runtime default. Find where the disablethp setting is read and applied in the runtime, and describe it briefly.

I timed `./make.bash` on our build box (32 cores) on 2026-09-20: median 2m41s over 5 cold-cache runs. Is there anything in src/make.bash or cmd/dist that would make a cold-cache build much slower than a warm one? Answer briefly.

Heads-up from infra: on our CI runners /tmp is a tmpfs capped at 512 MB, so go test runs that write large temporary files fail with 'no space left on device'. Set GOTMPDIR=/scratch/gotmp on those runners. Find where cmd/go reads GOTMPDIR and describe what it controls. Do not change code.

Correction from the infra team: the CI runners run Linux kernel 5.15, not 5.4. The seccomp rule blocking pidfd_open is unchanged. Does anything in the os package's pidfd support depend on the kernel version?
